### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A26 and A18 (the pair occurring within five steps of each other) averaged about 0.9 hours, with a median of about 0.93 hours and a middle half spanning roughly 0.83–0.99 hours. In the later window, the same interval averaged about 0.46 hours, with a median of about 0.46 hours and a middle half spanning roughly 0.41–0.51 hours — a reduction of about 0.45 hours, roughly half the earlier value. [TWAIT001]
- The whole distribution shifted down together: the quartiles and the spread (standard deviation about 0.13 hours before, about 0.08 hours after) all decreased, and the middle halves of the two windows do not overlap. The interval was observed in a similar share of traces in both windows — 47 of 200 traces (about 1 in 4) in each — so how often the pair occurred did not change. [TWAIT001]
- The difference is unusual for a stable process: it exceeds the differences seen in 1,999 of 2,000 random re-splits of the pooled data. [TWAIT001]
- Screening found no qualifying control-flow differences (0 items among 56 tested units, where about 0.28 would qualify by chance). The single qualifying item is in the time family, where only about 0.013 items would be expected by chance among 26 tested units — far above what an unchanged process typically produces. [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a change in timing: in the later window, the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A26 and A18 is about half of what it was in the earlier window (from about 0.9 hours to about 0.46 hours on average). The hypothesis rests on direct measurement of exactly this interval, consistency across all distribution components (mean, median, both quartiles and spread, with non-overlapping middle halves), comparable participation in both windows (about 1 in 4 traces in each), and a difference larger than in 1,999 of 2,000 random re-splits. The screening comparison also supports it: one qualifying time item against a chance expectation of about 0.013 is many times the expected count, while the control-flow family produced no items (0 of 56 units against about 0.28 expected). [TWAIT001]

Limitations: TWAIT measures elapsed time between consecutive completion events, not pure waiting or processing time, so the evidence shows a shorter interval between the two completions but cannot show what brought the shortening about. A difference in the make-up of the traces containing the pair (for example, different activities lying between the two completions) cannot be fully ruled out, although no structural difference was detected at the configured thresholds. [TWAIT001]

Other differences: none — no control-flow, participation or ordering differences qualified. [TWAIT001]
